- When sentiment is consistently low or negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >1.5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment changes sharply upward (e.g., +0.5+ in 1–2 days) with low news volume, model underreacts — increase forecast by 0.3–0.8% to match sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat for 3+ days, model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecast should be closer to 30-day moving average of prior 10 days.
- High news volume (≥3) with no sentiment change suggests model overreacts — dampen forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid noise-driven overfitting.
- If true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), model may be overestimating supply/demand — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment shifts.
- If true outcome is consistently above model (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), model may be underestimating sentiment — increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
